purpose: Authoritative-vendor review adding Mitti (formerly SafetyCulture) as a manufacturing-relevant EHS/quality/training/asset platform at spec-verified. Current provider documentation confirms a REST API, signed webhooks, service-user/user API tokens, site/access-aware permissions, incremental inspection sync, assets/custom fields, training progress events, actions/incidents, endpoint-specific throttling and the August 2026 SafetyCulture-to-Mitti API/domain transition. No credentials, customer data, production mutation, webhook registration or plant-network access were used.

systems.name: Mitti (formerly SafetyCulture)
systems.evidenceNote: Provider-owned Mitti documentation confirms HTTPS REST at api.mitti.com, bearer API tokens, service-user identities for long-running integrations, permission/access enforcement, modified-since inspection sync, signed HMAC-SHA256 webhooks, endpoint-specific 429/rate-limit behavior, asset/site/custom-field APIs, actions/incidents and training progress events. SafetyCulture rebranded to Mitti on 11 August 2026; api.mitti.com is the long-term host while api.safetyculture.io remains a documented transitional host with no shutoff date. No authenticated calls were made.

webhooks.vendorRequirement: user Administrator or service-user Override permissions: Manage all data for registration/receipt
webhooks.approvedPattern: customer-pre-registers webhook out of band; WFM runtime receives only the webhook verification secret and normal constrained read token

securityEvidenceBlockers: Before authentication evidence can advance, prove a dedicated Mitti service-user token whose effective permission set is read-only for the required domains and whose content/site access is limited to the approved organization/site scope; token creation defaults to all permissions selected and successful bearer authentication alone is not least-privilege evidence.

requiredPermissions: dedicated Mitti service-user API token for long-running integration; do not use a human token for shared production runtime
read-only permissions for approved inspections/templates, assets/sites, actions/incidents and training analytics/progress required by the customer workflow
bind organization and site/content access through Mitti permission sets, sharing/site membership and access rules; separate token per organization where applicable
pin api.mitti.com as the canonical host; treat api.safetyculture.io only as an explicitly configured transitional host during migration and never auto-follow cross-host redirects
do not grant Assets: Manage, user/group/platform administration, inspection mutation, schedule mutation, training assignment mutation or other write permissions to the normal WFM connector

do not let the WFM runtime retain or reuse the Administrator/Manage-all-data credential required for webhook setup; prefer REST polling/reconciliation or customer-controlled pre-registration with only the HMAC verification secret supplied to runtime
dataAvailableOrExpected: inspections/audits with stable audit/template IDs, created/modified times, scores, responses, site/asset references, media references and custom operational/quality/safety fields
templates and response structures used to interpret customer-specific inspection/SOP fields
assets with system ID, customer-defined code, type, site, status, media and typed custom fields including string, money and timestamp values
sites/location hierarchy and site-scoped access context where configured
actions/corrective tasks including assignment, due date, priority, status, site and asset linkage
incidents/issues including classification, status, assignment, site and corrective-action context; ingest only minimized non-health-sensitive fields required by WFM
training courses/lessons plus enrolment, completion, expiry, lesson progress and score events/analytics where the customer licenses Training
users/service-user-relevant identity references needed for correlation, subject to purpose limitation
inspection and training webhook events containing stable resource IDs, organization identity, event time and version
media metadata/links where a customer workflow explicitly needs evidence; avoid copying raw media unless necessary
schedules/recurring inspection work exist in the API but remain read-context only for WFM unless a future write use case is separately approved

freshnessLatency.scheduledSync: incremental inspection reads can filter by modified_after/modified_before and should checkpoint with overlap/reconciliation
freshnessLatency.webhooks: near-real-time best-effort only; duplicates, out-of-order delivery and loss are explicitly possible, with up to four retries roughly 100 seconds apart after receiver errors
freshnessLatency.mobileOffline: inspection webhooks fire only after mobile inspections synchronize to the Mitti server; source event time and server/ingestion time must therefore be preserved
freshnessLatency.training: webhook/event or API analytics freshness depends on product sync; do not equate completion event arrival time with qualification effective time unless customer policy does so

paginationDeltaEvents.inspectionDelta: use modified_after/modified_before plus deterministic field selection; default search returns up to 1000 inspections and is sorted by modified_at oldest-to-newest
paginationDeltaEvents.assetPagination: page_token / next_page_token with page_size 1-100 on documented list/search surfaces
paginationDeltaEvents.webhookDelivery: best-effort, duplicate and out-of-order; dedupe by webhook/resource/event identity and reconcile against authenticated incremental reads
paginationDeltaEvents.webhookSignature: HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body using the organization signature secret, compared with x-safetyculture-signature; legacy header name remains unchanged after rebrand
paginationDeltaEvents.webhookFallback: webhooks are a signal, not completeness proof; scheduled read reconciliation remains mandatory

rateLimitsAndRetries: documented common read limits include 200 requests per 60 seconds for inspection search and many training/assets-related API operations, but use endpoint-specific current vendor limits rather than a single global assumption
use bounded exponential backoff with jitter for retryable HTTP/network failures and do not retry non-idempotent mutation operations because WFM writes are disabled
webhook receiver must return promptly, authenticate before processing, deduplicate retries and rely on scheduled reconciliation for loss
versionsRegionsCustomFields: current developer portal labels API reference v1.0; endpoint families may carry their own /v1 paths and must be pinned/tested independently
single API host serves all regions according to current rebrand guidance; customer application/domain migration continues in stages through 2027
api.safetyculture.io remains operational as a transitional API host, but new WFM configurations should prefer api.mitti.com and fail closed on undocumented hosts
asset custom fields are typed and identified separately from labels; preserve field IDs/types and schema fingerprints so renamed labels do not silently remap data
inspection/template schemas are customer-configurable; map by stable item/entity IDs plus template/revision context rather than display text alone
automationOpportunities: join training completion/expiry and customer-approved competency evidence to WFM availability and production demand to flag likely qualification gaps before a shift locks
convert recurring quality/safety inspection failures and corrective-action backlog into staffing/training recommendations without ingesting unnecessary sensitive incident narratives
use asset/site inspection findings and action status to forecast maintenance/support labour demand and redeploy qualified available workers before downtime creates overtime or agency demand
combine inspection/quality outcomes with payable-time and production data to expose labour cost associated with rework, repeated defects, audit failure and corrective-action burden
use stable asset code/custom fields to reconcile Mitti assets to ERP/MES/CMMS equipment without brittle display-name matching
feed site-level compliance/training/asset readiness into manager and executive reporting while preserving source lineage and evidence time
future event-driven workflows can reduce latency, but the default connector should use signed events only after customer-controlled webhook bootstrap is separated from WFM runtime authority
savingsHypotheses: reduce overtime and agency labour by identifying expiring/missing training or competency evidence before assigning scarce production/maintenance work
reduce repeat defects and rework labour by linking recurring inspection failures and corrective actions to targeted training, staffing and process interventions
reduce downtime by aligning asset/inspection/action signals with available qualified maintenance or operations labour
reduce manual HSEQ/training reconciliation by using stable API identifiers, site hierarchy and incremental sync instead of spreadsheet exports
improve labour-to-quality and labour-to-downtime attribution by joining Mitti evidence with WFM payable-time/cost data while keeping Mitti timestamps as operational evidence rather than payroll truth

speed implementation for SafetyCulture customers during the Mitti migration by treating SafetyCulture/iAuditor as aliases of one canonical connector and explicitly handling the documented API-host transition rather than deploying duplicate integrations
dataGaps: Mitti is not authoritative for employment contracts, leave entitlement, payable time, payroll rules, agency commercials or complete production demand unless those are sourced from approved upstream systems
training completion/score is not automatically a regulated qualification or licence-to-work decision; customer policy and authoritative certification evidence remain controlling
incident/investigation records may contain health or special-category data and should be minimized to approved status/classification signals rather than copied wholesale

public documentation verifies the technical contract but no customer tenant has yet proven the exact least-privilege permission set, site hierarchy, custom template mappings or data volume behavior for this WFM connector
webhook registration requires elevated authority, so signed webhook capability exists but must not be enabled by giving the runtime broad administrator/manage-all-data credentials
custom inspection/template fields and asset fields can drift over time; schema fingerprinting and customer-approved mapping remain required
offline mobile sync can delay event arrival; late data may reconcile history but must not masquerade as a live state change
constraintsRisks: service-user token creation currently presents all permissions selected by default; deployment automation must explicitly verify the effective role/access rather than assuming a service user is safe

webhook creation/receipt requirements are overprivileged for the normal WFM runtime: a user needs Administrator or a service user needs Override permissions: Manage all data, which can edit/archive/delete data and override access rules

the SafetyCulture-to-Mitti rebrand introduced new canonical domains while legacy API/domain names remain valid during staged migration; duplicate connector records or automatic cross-host redirects could split lineage or weaken tenant/host pinning
API includes create/update/delete operations across assets, inspections, users/schedules and other domains; read intent does not make a broad token read-only
webhooks are not ordered or guaranteed and may duplicate; event-only processing would create silent data gaps

customer-configurable templates, custom fields, site access and sharing rules can create partial visibility that looks like missing data unless diagnostics distinguish authorization from source absence
current rate limits vary by endpoint and may change; adapters must respond to vendor headers and current documentation rather than hard-code one platform-wide quota
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Obtain an authorised Mitti trial/sandbox or customer-approved test organization. Create a dedicated service-user token with only the minimum read permissions and site/content access, then prove denied mutations, organization/site isolation, token expiry/rotation, paginated asset reads, modified-since inspection backfill, custom-field mapping and reconciliation after duplicate/out-of-order/missed events. Keep webhook registration out of the runtime credential plane; either use REST-only scheduled sync for the first live proof or have the customer pre-register a webhook and provide only the HMAC verification secret. Validate api.mitti.com as the pinned canonical host and exercise the documented api.safetyculture.io transition only as an explicit migration test, never via automatic cross-host redirect.
